title: Battenberg cake
subtitle: The classic marzipan-wrapped chequerboard sponge in pink and yellow
excerpt: A battenberg is two almond sponges baked together, cut into strips, glued with apricot jam into a two-by-two chequerboard, and wrapped tightly in marzipan. The method is logical and the result is impressive; the work lies in cutting the sponge strips to a consistent size so the pattern reads clearly at every slice.
sourceNotes: Battenberg cake is a British classic, named in 1884 to honour the marriage of Queen Victoria's granddaughter to Prince Louis of Battenberg. The chequerboard pattern wrapped in marzipan has been the defining feature since the earliest published versions. The method described follows the standard British home-baking approach.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the sponges the day before and cool completely. Wrap and store at room temperature. Assemble with marzipan on the day.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 170 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 155 degrees Celsius. Bake on the middle shelf.

glossaryTerms.definition: The technique of rolling marzipan into a thin rectangle, brushing the outside of the assembled chequerboard sponge with apricot jam, and rolling the sponge tightly inside the marzipan sheet so the join sits at the base. Trim the ends cleanly to reveal the pattern.

content.text: A battenberg works because both sponge colours are baked in the same tin at the same time, separated by a foil divider, so they are identical in height and density. The
holds the strips together and is what gives the cake its distinctive look at the cut end.
Preheat the oven to 170 degrees Celsius. Grease and line a 20 cm square tin with a foil divider down the middle to create two equal rectangles.

Beat the butter and sugar together until pale and fluffy, then add the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour and baking powder. Divide the batter equally into two portions by weight. Stir almond extract into one portion and vanilla extract into the other, then colour the almond portion pink with a small amount of gel food colouring.
Spoon each colour into its half of the tin. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely before cutting.
Trim each sponge into a neat rectangle. Cut each rectangle into two equal strips of the same height and width. You should have two pink strips and two yellow strips.

Brush the long sides of a pink strip with warm apricot jam and press a yellow strip against it. Brush the top of this double strip and press the second pink-yellow pair on top in the opposite order so the colours alternate: pink-yellow on the bottom, yellow-pink on top.

Roll the marzipan on a surface lightly dusted with icing sugar into a rectangle wide enough to wrap around the whole block. Brush the outside of the assembled block with jam, then roll it in the marzipan so the join falls at the base. Trim the ends to reveal the chequerboard.
